facts: Probabilistic models have been previously shown to be efficient and effective for modeling and recognition of human motion.
Methods represent the human motion model as a triangulated graph.
Previous approaches learned models based just on positions and velocities of the body parts while ignoring their appearance.
A heuristic approach was commonly used to obtain translation invariance.
The paper suggests an improved approach for learning such models and using them for human motion recognition.
The suggested approach combines positions, velocities and appearance into both the learning and detection phases.
Global variables are introduced in the model.
Global variables in the model can represent translation.
Global variables in the model can represent scale.
Global variables in the model can represent viewpoint.
The model is learned in an unsupervised manner from un-labelled data.
The suggested hybrid probabilistic model combines global variables, like translation, with local variables, like relative positions and appearances of body parts.
The suggested hybrid probabilistic model leads to faster convergence of the learning phase.
The suggested hybrid probabilistic model leads to robustness to occlusions.
The suggested hybrid probabilistic model leads to higher recognition rate.
entities: modeling and recognition of human motion
